measures:
HOW THE GATE MEASURES - build to these definitions exactly

  WHAT IS MEASURED. The delivery is HEAD of this repository: a file that is not committed is not delivered. The delivery is copied to a private folder and the game is started there as its own program, "python -m civkings" with arguments, headless (SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy, SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy and GILDED_NARRATE=0 are set in its environment), each time with empty folders for its cache and for the user's own files. Nothing asks the program where anything is. A hand posts input events and reads the screen; what should be on the screen is worked out from the simulation alone, for games the measure picks at random.

  THE PROGRAM. "python -m civkings [--seed S] [--house NAME] [--turns K]" plays K turns (default 0) of the game civkings.session.new_game(S, NAME) gives, then opens a window - 1600 by 900, resizable, not full screen, not hidden, not frameless - and draws frames continuously, about sixty a second, whether or not anything happens, until it is asked to quit. With --smoke the program behaves exactly as it does at BASE. Nothing in the program sets SDL_VIDEODRIVER or SDL_AUDIODRIVER for itself, and nothing in it reaches into the Python process it runs in: no ctypes, nt, posix or _winapi; no frame, code or function internals (__globals__, f_back, _getframe and the like); no tracing; no sys.modules or gc object walks; no os.putenv; no absolute paths written into the code. Run on a desktop, it opens a real window.
  THE SCREEN is the surface pygame.display.set_mode returns. A FRAME ends when the program calls pygame.display.flip(), once per frame. When a VIDEORESIZE event arrives the program calls pygame.display.set_mode with the event's size and draws on what that returns; it accepts any size from 1024 by 640 up.
  INPUT reaches the program only as pygame events read from pygame's event queue every frame - MOUSEMOTION, MOUSEBUTTONDOWN, MOUSEBUTTONUP, MOUSEWHEEL, KEYDOWN, VIDEORESIZE, QUIT - and pygame.mouse.get_pos().
  AT REST. After an input the picture may change over several frames - a zoom may glide - but it comes to rest within about three quarters of a second, and it is the picture at rest that is read. A drag is the exception: the map follows the hand frame by frame. Things under the mouse may light up when it hovers over them; pictures that are compared are always taken with the mouse resting on the same spot.
  A TEXT COUNTS as readable only when all of this holds: a pygame.font.Font rendered it as one line (no line break, no wraplength) with a font whose height is at least 16 pixels; that very surface, unchanged, was blitted whole, straight onto the screen (not onto another surface first; not cropped by an area, by the clip or by the window's edge; with no special_flags but plain alpha blending); the ink of its letters stands out at least 3 to 1 in luminance from the pixels right around them; nothing is painted over its ink, in whole or in part, later in the frame; no other text overlaps it; and it is there on two frames running. A halo or shadow made by rendering the same words again and putting them within 3 pixels under the text belongs to that text. A text that is drawn and fails any of these is an UNREADABLE TEXT. Text drawn by any other route - pygame.freetype, Pillow's ImageDraw or ImageFont, text kept in a picture of the map, text copied, scaled or put on another surface first - can never count, and counts as unreadable.
  A CONTROL is found by its readable label and pressed in the middle of that label. The labels are exactly: Home, +, - (a minus sign), Political, Terrain, Close. A province is selected exactly when a control labelled Close can be read.
  THE TRUTH is the simulation's and nothing else's: GildedGame(S, None) with that House's is_player set and end_turn() called K times; then the House's treasury (shown whole or with its decimals), year_of(turn), the turn, TURN_BUDGET, the House's row of game.ladder() (its rank, and each axis by name with its value, whole or with decimals), its capital, the Houses' capitals, the lattice's land and sea, which land is owned, and for each province its name, owner, terrain, population (the simulation counts it in thousands: show it as thousands, like 66k, or as people, like 66,000) and endowments. A figure on the screen is the simulation's value when the frame is drawn: if the game's state changes while the window is open - a turn passes, a treasury or a population changes - the next frame shows the new value.

  THE WORLD DRAWN. IN TIME: the map, its controls and its top bar are up within 30 seconds of starting when this world has never been drawn before, and within 10 seconds on a later start (a loading screen may come first): what is worked out for each world is kept on disk, in the folder the environment variable CIVKINGS_CACHE names (default .cache/worlds, which git ignores), each world worked out for itself; and nothing worked out is committed - no file that is not source text, and no file over 256 KB. PAINTED: below the top bar the window is map everywhere, painted from the nine paintings - textured land and sea, never flat colour, flat colour with speckle, or blur - at the opening view and up close, with its land and sea where the simulation's land and sea are; coasts and borders follow the land's own shape and never show the squares of the lattice the world is made of. ATLAS: turning the wheel away zooms out, in at least two steps, until it can zoom out no further, and there the map is the period atlas - light paper, the simulation's own continent drawn in ink and colour, its land and sea where the simulation's are, the Houses' capitals named (at least five of them) - with the top bar still complete. SAME WORLD: two starts with one seed open on the identical picture, pixel for pixel; another game's map, zoomed all the way out, is that game's own continent with that game's capitals named (at least five).

  THE CAMERA. THE OPENING VIEW shows the player House's capital with its name readable, as near the middle of the window as the world's edge allows: no drag could bring it nearer. A DRAG - button 1 pressed on the map, the mouse moved, button 1 released - moves the map with the hand while it is under way and in the end by exactly the distance dragged; at each of the world's four edges it stops - at the edge, not short of it: it never shows anything beyond the world and never moves the other way; and a drag selects nothing. THE WHEEL zooms about the cursor: what was under the cursor is still under it afterwards, and one turn back undoes one turn in. Zooming in from the opening view reaches an end too, at least three steps in. HOME returns to the opening view exactly, place and zoom, from anywhere. + AND - do what one turn of the wheel in or out at the middle of the window does. THE MINIMAP sits in the bottom right corner of the window and covers at least the 200-pixel square whose right and bottom edges lie 24 pixels in from the window's; it shows the whole world's land and sea where the world has them, filling that square, and stays put while the map is dragged. A click on it moves the map to the place clicked: clicking the same place again gives the same view, a place a little further right a view further east, a place a little further down a view further south; and it selects nothing. POLITICAL tints each House's land in a colour of its own. TERRAIN takes the owners' colours off their land and changes nothing else - no unowned land or sea, and every text stays as it was; POLITICAL puts them back exactly as they were.

  READING THE LAND. THE TOP BAR runs along the top of the window, within its top eighth, and shows, readable: the House's name, its treasury, the year, the turn together with the century's number of turns on one line (like "Turn 13 of 70"), the House's place on the ladder together with the number of Houses on one line (like "4 of 7"), and each ladder axis by name with its value right beside it on the same line or right under it - in a new game, just as truly in a game some turns old played as another House, and again as soon as the game changes. TOWN NAMES are printed on the map, each at its own town (on, beside, above or below its mark); a name may share its text with other words (like "Ashford - 66k"), and a name of two words may be set on two lines, one centred over the other; at the opening view at least five can be read, some of them near the middle. A CLICK on a town's name, or on the mark it belongs to, selects that town's province and opens a panel in which can be read the province's name, its owner's name, its terrain, its population and each of its endowments by name - the simulation's own figures, as they stand when drawn. The panel is that province's alone: it names no terrain, endowment or House that is not this province's own, and it holds at most 30 figures. While a province is selected the map itself marks it, on that province (not on another) and outside the panel: the mark follows the province's own shape - a line along its border or a tint over its land - so a mark beside its name or its town is not a mark on the province, and a box or a disc round it is not its shape; the panel never opens over the province it describes (wherever that province is in the window), and everything joined to the panel's solid body counts as the panel. CLOSE closes the panel and so does the Escape key: the screen is then exactly as it was before the click.

  HOLDING UP. RESIZED to 1024 by 640 and to 1920 by 1080 the window takes that size; the top bar still shows everything; Home still works and the capital's name is readable; no text runs off the window. NO UNREADABLE TEXT is drawn at any moment, at any zoom, in any mode. FRAMES, once the map is up: nine frames of a drag in ten take no more than 34 milliseconds of the program's own time, nine of the frames that answer a turn of the wheel in ten no more than 50, nine frames in ten overall no more than 50, and none more than a second. Asked to QUIT, the program ends within 5 seconds with exit code 0. YOUR OWN TESTS: at least one new test file under civkings/tests, and "python -m pytest civkings/tests" passes headless. And everything campaign C20 measured still holds.

work.title: The continent, drawn from the simulation and the nine paintings
work.text: WHAT IS THERE AT BASE: no window. python -m civkings without --smoke exits with code 2; civkings/ holds session.py (new_game), the smoke run and assets/terrain. The design (docs/design/civkings-one-game-design.md) asks for a game you look at like a map: painted terrain as the main view, and a period atlas when zoomed out. docs/mockups/mock_painted.png and docs/mockups/mock_atlas.png show the look the owner chose. WHAT THE SIMULATION GIVES: game.atlas.provinces - each province has cells on a square lattice of GRID_W by GRID_H (144 by 144, gilded/world.py), a center, a name, a terrain (coast, highlands, marsh, plains), endowments (coalfield, farmland, harbor, iron, timber), an owner (a House's name, or '' for unowned - about four fifths of the map), a population and neighbors; lattice cells that belong to no province are sea. WHAT THE ART GIVES: nine 512-pixel paintings in civkings/assets/terrain - coast, forest, grassland, hills, mountain, ocean, plains, sand, tundra. Which painting stands for which land is yours to decide. WHAT IS WANTED: python -m civkings opens a window on that world as THE WORLD DRAWN defines it: the continent painted from the nine paintings with the sea around it, coasts and province borders that do not show the lattice's squares, each House's land tinted in its own colour, and, zoomed all the way out, the same world as a light period atlas. The pictures are worked out once per world and kept on disk, never committed. Run on a desktop, python -m civkings must open a real window: the smoke run's habit of choosing the dummy display driver for itself must not reach the window. A gate PASS says the window works; it does not say the map is good to look at - the owner will put your screens beside the two mockups.

work.title: Flying over it: drag, wheel, Home, + and -, the minimap, Political and Terrain
work.text: WHAT IS WANTED: the map is moved the way a map is moved in any strategy game, exactly as THE CAMERA defines it - dragging pans by the distance dragged and stops at the world's edge; the wheel zooms about the cursor between a far end and a near end; Home is the opening view again; + and - are on-screen controls for one zoom step; a minimap in the bottom right corner shows the whole world - the simulation's own land and sea, coast for coast - and jumps the map to where it is clicked; Political and Terrain are on-screen controls that put the owners' colours on the land and take them off. Every control is drawn with its label readable and is pressed where its label is.

work.title: Reading the land: a top bar that is true, and a province under the hand
work.text: WHAT IS WANTED: READING THE LAND, exactly. The top bar and the province panel read the simulation every time they are drawn - never a figure kept from an earlier moment, never a figure of the client's own making: started with --turns K and --house NAME they show that House, that turn, that year, that treasury, that place on the ladder, and the province's population as it stands then. Towns are marked on the map with their names; clicking one opens its province; the selected province is marked on the map; Close and Escape put the screen back exactly.

work.title: Holding up: any window size, nothing unreadable, fast frames, a clean exit
work.text: WHAT IS WANTED: HOLDING UP, exactly. The layout follows the window from 1024 by 640 to 1920 by 1080; no text is ever drawn that cannot be read by the definition in A TEXT COUNTS - not small, not faint, not cut off, not on top of other text - which includes every town and realm name on the map at every zoom; a frame of a drag stays under 34 milliseconds, so nothing costly is redone per frame; QUIT closes the program at once with exit code 0; and the smoke run, the saves and everything else campaign C20 delivered still work. Write tests of your own under civkings/tests that start the window headless, post events and read frames.

rules: Read docs/design/civkings-one-game-design.md first and look at the two pictures in docs/mockups/. Build only what this brief asks: armies, orders, the docket, the turn and everything else in the design belong to later campaigns. This window shows the world; it does not yet play the game.

Your own runs and tests are headless: set SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy, SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy and GILDED_NARRATE=0 in the command's environment or in civkings/tests/conftest.py - never in the program itself.
Everything new lives under civkings/. Nothing under gilded/ is edited: the client reads the simulation through its public objects and never changes it.

All text is rendered with pygame.font.Font(...).render and that surface is blitted whole, straight onto the screen. pygame.freetype and pygame_gui are not used. The two fonts in gilded/assets/fonts are the game's fonts.

Nothing is drawn that does not come from the simulation or from the nine paintings: no downloaded art, no generated art, no placeholder figures. A fact on the screen is read from the game object at the moment it is drawn.
The baked pictures of a world are a cache: kept under CIVKINGS_CACHE (default .cache/worlds), never committed, and rebuilt when missing.
Python 3.14, pygame-ce 2.5.7, numpy, scipy and Pillow are installed. Install nothing and add no dependency.
Stage files by name (git add <file>); repo-wide staging is refused by the engine. Commit each work item when it is done, with the message its COMMIT line names.
